To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
hybrid cells derived from human breast epithelial and cancer cells show differential TLR4/TLR9 signaling and that this signaling is involved in the regulation of the migratory behavior.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of TLR signaling in hybrid cell models and the identification of potential targets for the development of novel therapeutic strategies.
the development of hybrid cells as a model for the analysis of the interaction of tumor cells with cells of the immune system.
the role of TRLs in breast cancer cells and breast epithelial cells and the influence of their signaling on tumor progression and metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TLR4 signaling in hybrid cells is not as strong as in the parental cancer cells and that TLR9 signaling in hybrid cells seems to be more important than in the parental cancer and epithelial cells.
hybrid cells derived from human breast cancer cells (MDA-MB-435) and human breast epithelial (M13SV1) cells exhibit differential TRL4 and TLR signaling.
the hybrids are a suitable model to study the role of TRL4 and TLR signaling and the role of TIR domains in breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TLRs can act as both tumor suppressors and tumor promoters.
the TLR signaling in hybrid cells is more similar to breast epithelial cells than to breast cancer cells.
the M13-MDA435-1 hybrid cell line exhibits a TLR4 signaling pathway, while M13-MDA-435-3 cells exhibit a TLR9 pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that

hybrid cells derived from human breast cancer cells (MDA-MB-435) and human breast epithelial (M13) cells can be useful tools to study TLR4 and 9 signaling and to investigate the role of TRLs in breast cancer.
TLR4 and 9 signaling in hybrids is more robust than in parental cells.
TLR4 and/or TLR9 signaling in hybrid cells may be a useful tool in cancer therapy.
